items.title: US and Iran hold first talks since June after Trump's 'annihilation' threat
items.description: The talks are the first since a ceasefire collapsed in June, with the sides exchanging fire intermittently.

items.title: Reports of violence against women in Gaza surge, UN agency finds
items.description: The UN Population Fund also says there has been a "severe escalation" in the number of early and forced marriages.

items.title: Eleven killed in mass shooting at house in South Africa
items.description: One of those killed is believed to be a pregnant woman, police said.

items.title: Trump administration accuses banned media outlets of 'falsehoods' ahead of court hearing
items.description: The US Justice Department's response to a lawsuit filed by CNN, Politico and MS NOW also cites national security.

items.title: More than 170,000 respiratory cases recorded in haze-choked Indonesia
items.description: More than 40,000 of the cases – which range from mild coughs to pneumonia – involve toddlers.

items.title: Hurricane Polo intensifies into rare category 5 storm off the coast of Mexico
items.description: The storm's sudden intensification is "truly remarkable", the US hurricane monitoring agency said.

items.title: Playing loud music on the bus? That will cost you hundreds of dollars in Singapore
items.description: Authorities are cracking down on "disruptive behaviours" including eating onboard and putting feet on seats.

items.title: US to build two military bases in Greenland under new deal with Denmark
items.description: The defence deal signed at the UN General Assembly also re-affirms Denmark's sovereignty over its semi-autonomous Arctic territory.

items.title: Trump meets US-backed Venezuelan president for first time since Maduro seized
items.description: Rodriguez was handpicked by Trump as leader of Venezuela was arrested and taken to the US

items.title: Angry Anderson, rock star who soundtracked Kylie's wedding in Neighbours, dies aged 79
items.description: He fronted the rock band Rose Tattoo, but became best known for his solo hit Suddenly.

items.title: Ukraine anger as EU removes Russian oligarchs from sanctions list
items.description: Alisher Usmanov and Mikhail Fridman both have close ties to President Putin, and Kyiv said the move sent Moscow the wrong signals.

items.title: How Ceuta, football and Israel are shaping Morocco's election
items.description: Young voters are being courted with football slogans, promises of jobs and anti-Israel rallying calls.

items.title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak
items.description: Scientists say the developing El Niño is now the strongest on record with weather impacts already being felt around the world.

items.title: US judge blocks deportation of DoorDash driver shot by ICE
items.description: The delivery driver was transferred from a hospital to a detention centre after the shooting on Sunday.

items.title: Lindsay Clancy's lawyer asks judge to investigate juror and check his phone
items.description: The attorney wants the court to look at the juror's mobile phone use and answers on questionnaires.

items.title: Sri Lanka court convicts 15 men over deadly Easter Sunday bombings
items.description: Three churches and three luxury hotels were targeted in the 2019 attacks which killed 270.

items.title: Autopsy shows Hayden Panettiere died from a drug overdose
items.description: The death of the child star - who had fentanyl, Xanax, a muscle relaxant and antipsychotic medication in her system - was ruled an accident.

items.title: Huge data centres rise at 'China speed' to power its AI ambitions
items.description: The BBC visits Inner Mongolia, an unlikely frontier in Beijing's AI race with Washington.

items.title: 'I have never felt heat like that' - a survivor on watching 33 cellmates die in Nigeria
items.description: The BBC goes inside the prison where prisoners were trapped in stifling, cramped conditions.

items.title: Lithuania ready to 'fight back' but has evacuation plans in face of Russia threats, PM tells BBC
items.description: Sinkevičius told BBC Newsnight Lithuanians feel "constantly threatened" by Moscow, but the nation was prepared to "fight back" if attacked.
